newsitem.title: USA: EU 95 pct near to deal on stability pact - Mersch.
newsitem.headline: EU 95 pct near to deal on stability pact - Mersch.

text.p: The European Union is 95 percent near to agreeing on a stability pact which will oblige members of monetary union to stick to fiscal discipline after a single currency is launched in 1999, a member of the EU's powerful monetary committee said on Monday.

Yves Mersch, treasury director at the Luxembourg finance ministry, noted at a conference that EU finance ministers had agreed last weekend in Dublin on the principle of a stability pact with sanctions for those running excessive budget deficits.

"The sanctions will not be left to haggling. We are trying to have a presumption that once a country has an excessive deficit it will be sanctioned unless it takes active steps" to change the situation, Mersch said.
"We are up to 95 percent close to agreement," he said.

EU finance ministers have asked the monetary committee to come up with proposals on the details of how to run a stability pact ahead of hoped-for approval by EU heads of state at a summit in Dublin in December.
